content:
incident-bot: Pager: billing-usage-anomaly triggered at 2026-04-04T02:13:09Z for prod-billing. Severity: P2. Volume spike and UI mismatches observed.
Maria Chen: Got the page, investigating. UI shows some customers with inflated usage and others with zeros. Invoices queued but not generated for today.
Jon Park: Oncall handoff in 15. Maria, any preliminary root cause?
Maria Chen: Not yet. Initial hypothesis: aggregator job lag + a memcache eviction causing stale aggregates. Logs show a lot of 504 to /metrics/emit around 02:05Z.
ops-sre: I can retime the aggregator to replay from 02:00 if needed. Which job key?
Maria Chen: job=usage-aggregator-prod-1. Also seeing repeated write errors to billing-ledger: `write timeout after 5s` in the ledger worker logs.
Nora Li: I'm seeing a backlog on the Kafka topic `usage-events` — consumer lag jumped to ~1.2M messages around 02:04Z. Could be a consumer restart or GC stall.
Lee Patel: Thanks — customer impact assessment needed. Which customers are impacted? Any high-revenue ones?
Anya Gomez: Preliminary list: three enterprise customers in EU with large volumes, a cohort of small dev orgs who rely on dashboard. Customer success on standby to prepare notifications.
Jon Park: I'm taking over in 10. Maria, please capture current mitigation steps and a short customer-facing blurb we can push to status page.
Maria Chen: Mitigations in progress: 1) scaled up usage-consumer pool x2; 2) restarted ledger-writer process with increased timeouts; 3) kicked off a targeted replay for topic partition 4.
Maria Chen: Quick logs snippet:
```
[2026-04-04T02:05:12Z] ledger-writer ERROR write timeout after 5000ms, attempt=3
[2026-04-04T02:05:13Z] usage-aggregator WARN consumer lag=1,234,567 partition=4
[2026-04-04T02:06:09Z] kafka-client INFO rebalancing, reason=broker-down
```
ops-sre: Restarted ledger-writer on host rwd-ledger-03, configured socket timeout=15s. Consumer pool scaled to 6 -> 12 instances. Starting replay for p4 now.
billing-bot: Invoice engine queue size: 8,432 -> previous normal: <200. Next invoice batch run scheduled in 40m.
Maria Chen: Likely cause: transient broker flapping led to consumer rebalance and backlog. Combined with ledger timeouts, invoices were delayed and dashboard aggregates stale.
Jon Park: OK I'll own customer comms while Maria continues on root cause. Maria — if the replay finishes, can you validate aggregates before we re-enable invoice batch?
Maria Chen: Yes. I'll run a reconciliation query after replay completes. Query I'll run:
```sql
SELECT customer_id, SUM(tokens) as tokens_today
FROM reconciled_usage
WHERE event_day='2026-04-04'
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY tokens_today DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Nora Li: Replay progress: ~22% after 10m. ETA ~35m. Consumer liveness looks stable now.
Anya Gomez: Drafting customer note now. Suggested short blurb for status page: "Investigating an issue causing delayed invoice generation and incorrect usage display for some accounts. No charges have been processed incorrectly; we are replaying events and will provide updates within 1 hour." Thoughts?
Lee Patel: Add: we’ll notify impacted customers directly and provide a reconciliation once complete. Also include potential ETA for resolution if replay finishes.
Jon Park: I want a slightly more conservative ETA. Use 2 hours to finish reconciliation and send a post-incident summary within 24 hours.
Anya Gomez: Copy for status page (final):
"We are investigating an incident affecting billing usage displays and invoice generation for a subset of customers. Our engineers have scaled consumers and replayed backlog events. We expect to complete reconciliation and resume normal invoice processing within 2 hours. Impact: affected customers may see delayed invoices or inconsistent usage totals in the dashboard. No customers have been charged incorrectly. We will update this status within 60 minutes and provide a full reconciliation report within 24 hours."
Maria Chen: Replay complete at 2026-04-04T04:01Z. Running reconciliation now.
Maria Chen: Reconciliation results: mismatches found for 87 customer accounts (mostly EU-region high-volume). The ledger lacked ~3.2M tokens aggregated due to 3-minute write window where writer timed out. We've created a patch to backfill deltas and will run it now.
ops-sre: Backfill job started: backfill-billing-deltas-20260404 partitioned across 12 workers. Monitoring.
billing-bot: Backfill progress: 12% (380k tokens applied).
Jon Park: Preparing customer-facing email for impacted customers — Anya, add specifics and list of IDs. Maria, need validation steps post-backfill to confirm ledgers match event stream.
Maria Chen: Validation: run the reconciled query and compare to source events count. I'll attach a checksum sample.
Maria Chen: Sample checksum: customer ABC123 pre-backfill: 998,432 tokens, post-backfill: 1,034,210 tokens, delta applied: 35,778 tokens.
Anya Gomez: Email draft to impacted customers (short):
"Hi <customer>,
We’re reaching out to let you know we experienced a temporary issue that caused usage totals to be under-represented or delayed in your dashboard, and invoice generation was paused while we resolved the backlog. We have applied a reconciliation for 2026-04-04 and you may see updated usage / an adjusted invoice. No incorrect charges were processed. If you have billing concerns, reply here or open a ticket and CC your customer success rep."
Lee Patel: Good. Also include a line offering a one-time credit if the correction results in unexpected charges and ask CS to triage requests.
Jon Park: Status page update posted: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/XXXX — message matches Anya's final text.
billing-bot: Invoice queue now at 1,020 and decreasing. Next batch run in 10m.
Maria Chen: Post-backfill reconciliation shows ledger and event stream aligned for top 50 accounts. Full-run verification in progress.
Nora Li: Consumer lag back to normal. Broker cluster is stable after an auto-replace of broker-07. We should add better alerting on small transient broker flaps.
ops-sre: Noted — will open a follow-up to tune Kafka alerts and ledger writer backoff.
Anya Gomez: Customer notifications queued: 87 emails targeted, CS reps notified in #customer-success.
Jon Park: Handoff note: I'm leaving oncall in 20. @Nora Li will be next-oncall for billing path — Nora, confirm you can take postmortem lead and coordinate the 24-hour reconciliation report.
Nora Li: Confirmed, taking postmortem lead. Will coordinate with Maria, Lee, and Anya for timeline and writeups.
Maria Chen: Final internal note for thread: root cause = transient broker flapping -> consumer rebalance -> consumer lag -> ledger-writer timeouts during high write window -> backlog and stale dashboard aggregates. Mitigations: scaled consumers, restarted writer with increased timeouts, replayed events, backfilled deltas, posted status and customer notifications.
Jon Park: Great work team. Leaving oncall now. If any customer escalations, page me.
incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P3 at 2026-04-04T05:00Z. Follow-up tasks created: #INC-1842506789-postmortem (assignee: Nora Li).
Nora Li: I'll schedule postmortem doc and include runbook changes (kafka alert tweaks, ledger retry/backoff, invoice queue threshold).
